reading.body:
CyrusOne's Sterling campus publishes 116 MW of IT capacity, the second-largest disclosed figure in Virginia, in a state where only 25 of 330 mapped facilities publish any capacity at all.

That gap is the real finding. Virginia's 25 disclosing facilities total 1,603 MW, and Sterling alone accounts for 7.2% of it. The other 305 mapped facilities carry no public capacity figure, so the state's published load is a floor rather than a total. Any estimate of Virginia data center demand built from disclosed numbers understates what is physically there.

The campus itself reads as mixed-use rather than AI-specific. Its 1,177,019 square feet of technical space against 116 MW works out to roughly 98 watts per square foot, a density consistent with general workloads. The estimate of about 290 racks and 2,320 accelerators depends on assumed figures of 400 kW per rack and 8 accelerators per rack, which are modeling choices, not published specifications. CyrusOne lists no certifications for the campus.

What the data cannot settle is whether this capacity serves AI training. Power source, grid interconnection, actual workload mix, and any announced expansion are all absent. The published facts establish size and disclosure status, not how the campus is used or whether it can be powered at that load.
